levels.title: Basic
levels.scope: Angles, definitions, unit circle, fundamental identities

levels.title: Intermediate
levels.scope: Reduction, sum/difference, multiple-angle, product/sum, graphs, equations, triangles

cards.name: Degrees and radians
cards.photo_brief: Circle with angle π rad = 180° marked and a sector of 1 radian highlighted
cards.description: Converts between the two angle units. π rad equals 180°.

cards.name: Arc length and sector area
cards.photo_brief: Sector of a circle with radius r, central angle θ, arc s labelled
cards.description: Valid only when θ is in radians.

example.problem: r = 6, θ = π/3. Find s and A.

cards.name: Right-triangle definitions
cards.photo_brief: Right triangle with opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to angle θ
cards.description: Defines the three basic ratios for an acute angle θ.

example.problem: Legs 3 and 4, hypotenuse 5. θ is opposite the leg 3. Find sin θ, cos θ, tan θ.
example.solution: sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5, tan θ = 3/4.

cards.name: Reciprocal and quotient identities
cards.photo_brief: Table linking sin, cos, tan with csc, sec, cot
formulas: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
cot θ = cos θ / sin θ
cards.description: Expresses all six functions through sine and cosine.

cards.name: Special angle values
cards.photo_brief: 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles with side ratios 1 : √3 : 2 and 1 : 1 : √2
cards.description: Exact values used throughout school and exam problems.

cards.name: Unit circle and signs by quadrant
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle with point (cos θ, sin θ), quadrants labelled with positive functions (I all, II sin, III tan, IV cos)
formulas: Point on unit circle: (cos θ, sin θ)
cards.description: Sine is the y-coordinate and cosine is the x-coordinate. Use the reference angle for the magnitude and the quadrant for the sign.

example.solution: Quadrant II, reference angle π/6. sin = 1/2, cos = −√3/2.

cards.name: Periodicity
cards.photo_brief: Sine wave with one period 2π highlighted, tangent with period π
cards.description: Sine and cosine repeat every 2π. Tangent and cotangent repeat every π.

cards.name: Even and odd properties
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle with angles θ and −θ mirrored across the x-axis
cards.description: Cosine is even. Sine, tangent, cotangent are odd.

cards.name: Pythagorean identities
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle with right triangle of hypotenuse 1 and legs cos θ, sin θ
cards.description: Follow from x² + y² = 1 on the unit circle. Used to find one function from another.

example.problem: sin θ = 3/5, θ in Quadrant II. Find cos θ.
example.solution: cos²θ = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25. Quadrant II gives cos θ = −4/5.

cards.name: Cofunction identities
cards.photo_brief: Right triangle with complementary angles θ and 90° − θ
cards.description: A function of an angle equals the cofunction of its complement.

cards.name: Reduction formulas
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle showing angles π − θ, π + θ, 2π − θ as reflections of θ
formulas: sin(π − θ) = sin θ;  cos(π − θ) = −cos θ;  tan(π − θ) = −tan θ
sin(π + θ) = −sin θ;  cos(π + θ) = −cos θ;  tan(π + θ) = tan θ
sin(2π − θ) = −sin θ;  cos(2π − θ) = cos θ;  tan(2π − θ) = −tan θ
sin(π/2 + θ) = cos θ;  cos(π/2 + θ) = −sin θ
cards.description: Reduces any angle to an acute angle. Determine the sign from the quadrant of the original angle.

cards.name: Sum and difference formulas
cards.photo_brief: Two adjacent angles A and B on the unit circle with their sum A + B
formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B
cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B
tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B) / (1 ∓ tan A tan B)
cards.description: Note the sign change in the cosine formula. Used to obtain exact values of non-special angles.

cards.name: Double-angle formulas
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle with angles θ and 2θ
cards.description: Special case of the sum formulas with A = B = θ. Choose the cosine form that matches the given quantity.

example.problem: sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5. Find sin 2θ and cos 2θ.

cards.name: Half-angle formulas
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle with angles θ and θ/2
formulas: tan(θ/2) = sin θ / (1 + cos θ) = (1 − cos θ) / sin θ
cards.description: The sign of the root is set by the quadrant of θ/2.

cards.name: Power-reducing formulas
cards.photo_brief: Graphs of sin²θ and cos²θ shifted around the midline 1/2
cards.description: Rewrites squares of sine and cosine without powers. Essential for integration.

cards.name: Triple-angle formulas
cards.photo_brief: Unit circle with angles θ and 3θ
cards.description: Express a triple angle through powers of a single function.

cards.name: Product-to-sum formulas
cards.photo_brief: Two waves multiplied and shown as the sum of two waves
formulas: sin A cos B = ½[sin(A + B) + sin(A − B)]
cos A cos B = ½[cos(A − B) + cos(A + B)]
sin A sin B = ½[cos(A − B) − cos(A + B)]
cards.description: Converts a product into a sum. Used to simplify expressions and integrate products.

cards.name: Sum-to-product formulas
cards.photo_brief: Sum of two waves shown as a product of a slow and a fast wave
formulas: sin A + sin B = 2 sin((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2)
sin A − sin B = 2 cos((A + B)/2) sin((A − B)/2)
cos A + cos B = 2 cos((A + B)/2) cos((A − B)/2)
cos A − cos B = −2 sin((A + B)/2) sin((A − B)/2)
cards.description: Converts a sum into a product. Used to factor expressions and solve equations.

cards.name: Auxiliary angle (harmonic) form
cards.photo_brief: Right triangle with legs a and b, hypotenuse R and angle φ
formulas: a sin x + b cos x = R sin(x + φ)
cos φ = a/R,  sin φ = b/R
cards.description: Combines a sine and a cosine of the same angle into one sine. Gives the maximum R and minimum −R.

example.problem: Write sin x + cos x as a single sine and find its maximum.
example.solution: R = √2, φ = π/4. sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + π/4). Maximum √2.

cards.name: Sinusoidal graph parameters
cards.photo_brief: Sine wave with amplitude, period, phase shift and midline annotated
cards.description: Reads the shape of a sine or cosine graph directly from its equation.

example.solution: y = 3 sin(2(x − π/2)) + 1. Amplitude 3, period π, shift π/2 right, midline y = 1, range [−2, 4].

cards.name: Inverse trigonometric functions
cards.photo_brief: Graphs of arcsin, arccos, arctan with restricted ranges highlighted
formulas: arcsin(−x) = −arcsin x;  arccos(−x) = π − arccos x;  arctan(−x) = −arctan x
cards.description: Each inverse returns a single angle from its restricted range.

cards.name: Solutions of basic trigonometric equations
cards.photo_brief: Horizontal line y = a intersecting a sine wave at repeating points
formulas: sin x = a  ⇒  x = (−1)ⁿ arcsin a + πn
cos x = a  ⇒  x = ± arccos a + 2πn
tan x = a  ⇒  x = arctan a + πn
sin x = 0: x = πn;  sin x = 1: x = π/2 + 2πn;  sin x = −1: x = −π/2 + 2πn
cos x = 0: x = π/2 + πn;  cos x = 1: x = 2πn;  cos x = −1: x = π + 2πn
n is an integer;  |a| ≤ 1 for sin and cos
cards.description: General solutions. Special cases are written in simplified form.

example.solution: sin x = 1/2, x = (−1)ⁿ π/6 + πn, i.e. x = π/6 + 2πn or x = 5π/6 + 2πn.

cards.name: Law of sines
cards.photo_brief: Triangle ABC with sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C and circumscribed circle of radius R
formulas: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R
cards.description: Relates each side to the sine of the opposite angle. Used when an angle–side pair is known.

cards.name: Law of cosines
cards.photo_brief: Triangle ABC with angle C between sides a and b
cards.description: Generalises the Pythagorean theorem for two sides and the included angle, or for three sides.

cards.name: Triangle area with sine
cards.photo_brief: Triangle with two sides and the included angle shaded
cards.description: Area from two sides and the included angle.

example.problem: a = 6, b = 8, C = 30°. Find the area.

cards.name: Fundamental trigonometric limits
cards.photo_brief: Graph of sin x / x approaching 1 near x = 0
cards.description: Valid with x in radians. Used to resolve 0/0 forms.

cards.name: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
cards.photo_brief: Cycle diagram: sin → cos → −sin → −cos → sin under repeated differentiation
cards.description: Valid with x in radians. Functions beginning with “co” have negative derivatives.

example.solution: Product rule: (x sin x)′ = sin x + x cos x.

cards.name: Derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions
cards.photo_brief: Graph of arctan with its derivative curve 1/(1 + x²)
cards.description: Combine with the chain rule for composite arguments.

cards.name: Basic trigonometric integrals
cards.photo_brief: Reverse of the derivative cycle diagram
formulas: ∫ cos x dx = sin x + C
∫ sec x tan x dx = sec x + C
∫ csc x cot x dx = −csc x + C
cards.description: Direct reversals of the derivative table.

cards.name: Integrals of tan, cot, sec, csc
cards.photo_brief: Graph of tan x with shaded area under the curve on [0, π/4]
formulas: ∫ tan x dx = −ln|cos x| + C = ln|sec x| + C
∫ cot x dx = ln|sin x| + C
∫ sec x dx = ln|sec x + tan x| + C
∫ csc x dx = −ln|csc x + cot x| + C
cards.description: Logarithmic results. The first two follow from substitution u = cos x and u = sin x.

example.problem: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to π/4 of tan x dx.
example.solution: [−ln(cos x)] from 0 to π/4 = −ln(√2/2) = ½ ln 2.

cards.name: Integrals giving inverse trigonometric functions
cards.photo_brief: Graph of 1/(1 + x²) with area under the curve equal to arctan
cards.description: Recognise the forms √(a² − x²) and a² + x² in the denominator.

cards.name: Integrals of sin²x and cos²x
cards.photo_brief: Graph of cos²x with area under the curve on [0, π]
cards.description: Obtained with the power-reducing formulas.

example.problem: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to π of cos²x dx.
